solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great performance — one of the best at school?

definitions.meaning: a brilliant, decisive move or achievement

definitions.text: one of the best at school?
definitions.meaning: a schoolmaster's cane stroke, one of the 'six of the best' once given as punishment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Six of the best' was the traditional caning in British schools, so one stroke of the cane delivered by a master is one of the best.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke of genius or brilliant move counts as a great performance.

clue.text: Mother wearing headgear? It's wrong way round, wise one!

indicators.note: wearing normally puts the wearer inside, but the clue says the arrangement is reversed so mother surrounds the headgear

parts.note: mama is a familiar word for mother
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A mother has put her hat on back to front, and someone points it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's wrong way round' warns that the usual reading of 'wearing' flips: the headgear goes inside MAMA instead of around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The title means great soul in Sanskrit and is given to a revered sage, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Tread softly — the Alsatian is roaming in the peaks

indicators.note: the peaks are the tops of the words, which in a down entry are their first letters

explanation.surface: A walker is told to step quietly because a dog is loose in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tread softly' reads as one instruction; 'Tread' alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step of a staircase is a tread, the flat part you put your foot on.

clue.text: Opening for the artillery in Maine coming up, with support guaranteed

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading upwards, so the state's letters turn round

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
a bra is a supporting undergarment
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Maine a gun port is being built, with its foundations certain.
explanation.definitionFit: The splayed opening in a castle or fortification wall that a cannon fires through.

clue.text: Creature that's formed in wax, say

definitions.meaning: a design stamped into wax to close a letter or document

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the flippered sea mammal and the impression pressed into sealing wax.

clue.text: He drifts vaguely into a universal movement

indicators.note: vaguely suggests the letters drift loosely into a different order

explanation.surface: A man wanders aimlessly into joining some worldwide campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'universal movement' suggests a political cause; it is the movement of the universe, whose expansion shows as this effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The shift of light towards longer wavelengths is evidence of galaxies moving apart across the universe.

clue.text: She shows understanding about most paintings

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the trimmed word

parts.note: ken means knowledge or range of understanding

indicators.note: most of means drop the final letter of the word for paintings

parts.note: art is a word for paintings collectively

explanation.surface: A woman displays an appreciation of most of a set of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a bare pronoun standing for any woman's name; 'most' removes the last letter of the paintings word before 'about' wraps the understanding word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so any woman bearing it is a 'she'.

clue.text: God's 19 one put on

parts.note: the answer to 19 across means an attitude or posture, and pose is a synonym
I is the Roman numeral one
to don is to put on clothing

explanation.surface: A god's posture is a pretence he puts on.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' points to 19 across; take a synonym of that answer, not the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of the sea, brother of Zeus.

clue.text: Stop pourin', so to speak?

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: pouring with rain is raining, here with its g dropped too

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a heavy downpour can be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in 'pourin'' matches the dropped g in RAININ', which sounds like the phrase meaning check.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull back on a horse's reins halts it, hence to restrain or check.

clue.text: Lead panel's part of the furniture

parts.note: to lead is to head, as in head a procession
a board is a flat panel of wood

explanation.surface: A sheet of lead forms a component of some fitted furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the metal, but it is the verb meaning to be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright board at the top of a bed is a component of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: A flower picked from border: honesty

indicators.note: the letters are plucked out of the run of words that follows, like a flower picked from a bed

explanation.surface: Someone picks a single honesty bloom from a flower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword slang for something that flows, a river; honesty is also a garden plant, which strengthens the flower picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, so in crosswords it is a flower; this one runs through Switzerland and France.

clue.text: Tenor's town topper?

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in music
urban means of the town or city

explanation.surface: A singer's hat worn about town is asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is jokingly anything worn on top of the head, here a wound headdress rather than a top hat.

clue.text: Come across from Switzerland covertly, can one?

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

indicators.note: covertly suggests the letters of the words are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether it is possible to slip in from Switzerland unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covertly' reads as sneaking over the border, but it disguises the letters of 'can one' as ANCEON; Switzerland's vehicle code is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something by luck is to come across it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Mount up and fall

definitions.meaning: to build up gradually, as interest does
to fall to someone, as a benefit or right comes to them

explanation.definitionFit: Both are dictionary senses: accumulating, and coming to someone as an advantage, as rights fall to an heir.

clue.text: Forcibly remove Tracy, sprawled over centre of seawall

indicators.note: over means the name's letters spread across the central piece
sprawled suggests the letters of the name lie spread out in a new order
the centre is the middle three letters of the word seawall

explanation.surface: A woman named Tracy lies sprawled across the middle of a sea defence, needing to be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawled' rearranges the name as CARTY, which 'over' spreads round the three central letters of the sea defence; the woman in the surface is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something off by force or in a vehicle is a phrasal-verb synonym for removing it.

clue.text: Brokenly, old king stands against northern fellow

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke
a don is a fellow or teacher at a university

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler is set beside a man from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands against' simply places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done intermittently, in fits and starts, is done brokenly.

clue.text: High-level stand-in chauffeur?

parts.note: a system that steers in place of a human driver, high up in the sky in an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-level' sounds like seniority but means at altitude; the 'chauffeur' is the system that flies the plane while the pilot rests.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic control system that guides an aircraft stands in for the human at the controls.

clue.text: Aficionado's time on continent producing free composition

parts.note: an aficionado is an enthusiast or fan
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A music lover's spell abroad produces a work free of strict form.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece in free form, following the composer's imagination rather than a set structure.

clue.text: Earl's in Italian city, acquiring new cheese

indicators.note: acquiring means the city gains a further letter at its end
in places the earl's letters within the city's name

parts.note: Parma is a city in northern Italy
E is the abbreviation for earl, and the 's supplies S

explanation.surface: A nobleman staying in an Italian city picks up a new cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is also home of the cheese, which makes the surface feel like a definition throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian grating cheese is a specific example of cheese.

clue.text: Winkle out article on the inner side, making flatter

indicators.note: on the inner side places the article inside the verb for extracting

parts.note: to winkle something out is to prise it out
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone digs out an object from inside to make it level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like 'more flat', but it is the verb meaning compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone is to heap compliments on them, close to commending them.

clue.text: Laurel by church can provide viewpoint

parts.note: Stan Laurel, of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A laurel tree beside a church might give a good spot to look from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' looks like the shrub but is the comedian Stan Laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or attitude on an issue, a synonym of viewpoint.

clue.text: Ranks of statuettes dispersed, apart from famous Pharaoh

indicators.note: dispersed means the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
apart from means the pharaoh's letters are taken out

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the best-known pharaoh

explanation.surface: Rows of little statues are broken up, leaving only one famous Egyptian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from' removes TUT from STATUETTES, leaving STAETES; 'dispersed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The estates of the realm are the social classes or orders, so estates are ranks of society.

clue.text: Free to choose an up-to-date motor within

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A

indicators.note: within places the motor inside the up-to-date word

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: Having a modern car makes you free to choose where you go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering from the menu dish by dish lets you pick each item freely rather than a set meal.

clue.text: Joint keeps irritating internally

indicators.note: internally means keep only the inside of the word, losing its two ends

parts.note: something that rankles goes on irritating or festering

explanation.surface: A sore joint goes on hurting from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' strips the outer letters R and S from RANKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between the foot and the leg.

clue.text: Bung odd bits of saplings on to …

indicators.note: odd bits are the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the following words

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction, continued in the next clue, to stake young trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next as one sentence; it means nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap or plug for a cask is a bung, a stopper for the hole.

clue.text: Aussie dustman who wanted to be alone

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for a refuse collector
the film star Greta, famous for the line 'I want to be alone'

explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a rubbish collector and the surname of the reclusive Swedish actress Greta.

clue.text: Cheese-paring on English holiday?

indicators.note: on, in a down entry, places the English letter after the trimmed cheese
paring means trimming off the cheese's last letter

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A miserly person economises on a national holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese-paring' reads as stinginess, but splits into cheese and an instruction to trim it by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is a festival or celebration, and in French usage a holiday, hence the question mark.

clue.text: … pile, of course, after onset of spring

indicators.note: after places the course word behind the opening letter
the onset is the beginning, so take the opening letter of spring

parts.note: a tack is a sailing course, or a course of action

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a heap of things, naturally, once spring begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as a phrase, but 'course' is the piece and 'of' just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of things placed one on another is a pile.

clue.text: Ms Fitzgerald's aboard second faulty tram — be wary!

indicators.note: aboard means riding inside, so the singer goes inside the rearranged vehicle
faulty means the letters of the word tram are not in working order

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A famous singer rides a second tram that has broken down, and is told to watch out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges the vehicle as MRAT so the singer can sit aboard it; the second-letter abbreviation leads the answer even though it comes later in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense that something is wrong is the idiom's meaning, hence to be suspicious or on guard.

clue.text: Organise team, creating a crowded alliance?

indicators.note: creating suggests the letters of the two words are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Getting a team together produces an alliance with a lot of members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'creating' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A household of three lovers is a jokingly crowded relationship, since two is company and three a crowd.
